subject: Renewal negotiation — BridgeBack: request for executive approval on concession stack
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@bridgeback.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Kline <jkline@bridgeback.health>
Date: Mon, 28 Oct 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — need flexibility on pricing/terms

Marcus,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. We ran the numbers on our side and the 
procurement committee has pushed back on the renewal numbers you sent — our usage has been 
flattish and we need either a material price reduction or credits for the last two quarters to 
justify the spend.

Concretely they asked for:
- 25% list discount for year 2 (we know that's steep)
- A one-time credit equivalent to Oct-Nov usage (~$42k)
- An SLA addendum with uptime warranty tied to credits if breached

We're a long-term customer and would prefer to stay, but this needs to be a realistic offer. Can you escalate? Our renewal is up 12/15.

—Elena
Head of Platform Ops
BridgeBack Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@bridgeback.health>
Cc: James Kline <jkline@bridgeback.health>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Oct 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — need flexibility on pricing/terms

Elena — thanks for the clarity and the timeline. I'm escalating internally and looping in my manager. 
We value BridgeBack and want to keep you on a path that makes sense financially for both sides.

Quick alignment from our side on asks and constraints:
- 25% off list is outside our standard save playbook without exec authorization.
- We can consider a blended approach: a one-time credit, a modest term-lift to a 2-year commitment, and a targeted SLA addendum.

Proposed concession stack for internal approval (what I'll ask for):
1) One-time credit: $35,000 applied to invoice at renewal
2) 15% discount on year-2 list pricing if BridgeBack signs a 24-month term today
3) SLA addendum: 99.5% uptime with a quarterly uptime credit schedule (capped at 10% of quarterly invoice)

I'll need executive sign-off for the discount and SLA exposure. Please confirm that the credit + 15% on year 2 + SLA addendum would be sufficient to proceed. If so, I'll submit for approval and include a short implementation/rollback plan.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Oct 2029 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — need flexibility on pricing/terms

Marcus — thanks for the draft. Two quick asks before escalation packet:
1) Neha — can you run an incremental margin impact on: (a) $35k one-time credit, (b) 15% off year 2 assuming estimated ARR of $950k, and (c) SLA exposure capped at 10% quarterly credits?
2) Marcus — include a short-risk memo on how SLA addendum is monitored and fallbacks (e.g., automatic fallback to standard region, usage-throttling options).

If numbers look OK, I can take to the commercial execs for a decision. We should also push for a technical checkpoint to lock SLA language.

—Soojin
Head of Deals | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Nov 2029 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — financial impact for BridgeBack concession stack

Soojin / Marcus,

I ran the rough P&L and margin impact: written assumptions attached. TL;DR: the package below is within our delegated authority conditional on exec sign-off for the SLA exposure.
- One-time credit: $35,000 — NRR impact reduces by ~3.7% across the renewal year given current churn profile.
- 15% year-2 discount on ~$950k ARR estimate → ~$142k off year-2 revenue. Net present delta over two years ~ $106k (after gross margin assumptions).
- SLA credit exposure: modeled as a worst-case 10% quarterly credit hitting two quarters → ~$48k payout; expected < $12k based on historical uptime.

Recommendation: Approve the proposed stack if the execs accept limiting SLA credit liability to a 12-month cap of $60k and require a 24-month term to earn the 15% year-2 discount.

Attaching: bridgeback_fin_model_v1.xlsx (stub) — I'll upload final numbers to the deal record.

—Neha
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@bridgeback.health>
Cc: James Kline <jkline@bridgeback.health>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Nov 2029 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Approved offer: BridgeBack renewal concession package (final)

Elena / James —

Thank you for your patience. After review with finance and deals, we have executive authorization to offer the following final concession package: 

1) One-time credit of $35,000 applied at renewal invoice (will appear as credit line item).
2) A 24-month term commitment starting at renewal. If BridgeBack signs the 24-month term by 12/10/2029, we will apply a 15% discount to year-2 list pricing.
3) SLA addendum offering 99.5% uptime; credits triggered per quarter, capped at 12 months total liability not to exceed $60,000. SLA language attached.

Attachments: bridgeback_renewal_offer_v3.pdf (proposal with line items), SLA_Addendum_BridgeBack.docx (legal language for SLA). Please review and confirm by reply. If you accept, we'll prepare DocuSign package and route for counter-signature.

Next steps from our side: 
- Legal will issue final addendum (copy enclosed) and send DocuSign by 11/25.
- Implementation/tech lead will schedule a short call to confirm monitoring and rollback procedures.

Hope this gets us across the line — happy to hop on a call with your procurement if helpful.

Best regards,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0192
Attachment stubs: bridgeback_renewal_offer_v3.pdf (pdf), SLA_Addendum_BridgeBack.docx (docx)
